tests.summary: Advisor tests: priority order, recheck computation, and 'unknown is not safe'
Orchestration tests: run_check with an injected (fake) GitHub client
CLI-level tests: exit codes, JSON output, commands that never touch the network
End-to-end-ish command tests: every CLI handler, with the outside world stubbed
Regression-cluster tests: grading, independence and credibility
Config loading/validation tests
Smoke tests for the two entry points that had no direct coverage
Hard-gate tests: gates must override a low score and never be bypassed silently
GitHub payload parsing tests (fixtures only - no network)
HTTP layer tests: cache TTL, stale fallback, failure handling (no external network)
Personal Impact, Core Feature Readiness and Systemic Critical Risk
Environment-detection tests: the layer that reads the *real* machine
Notification-channel tests: payload shape, failure handling, no secret leakage
Preflight and health-check tests (local filesystem only)
Code provenance tests: the five cases from the design brief, plus the rest
Repository hygiene: nothing important may be silently ignored or stale
Report rendering tests (plain-text console, no network)
Risk-engine tests: the scoring rules are the product, so they are pinned here
Rollback safety: the pre-update check that can block *executing* an update
Tests for the secret/privacy scanner - the guard needs its own guard
State persistence tests: update_state.json and watch_state.json
Updater mechanics: command building, snapshots, dry runs (nothing is executed)
Usage profile: levels, weights, detection and cluster -> feature attribution
Unit tests for the shared helpers - the layer every other module leans on
Version parsing/comparison tests - the part that must never be wrong
Watch-mode delta tests: only meaningful transitions may notify
